1.1.text: Inspector Irratino wanted to try bobbing for apples but he didn't want to mess up his hair, so instead he just hung out, and he saw that Leaf Collector Brown brought a collector's guidebook.

1.2.text: Inspector Irratino drew a marot card and immediately could tell that Cryptozoologist Cloud had a turkey leg. That's what the gruesome, terrifying weapon was!

1.3.text: Captain Slate was up on the moon, 238,900 miles away, minding her own business. "And yet, still I'm a suspect!"

1.4.text: Chef Aubergine was almost kicked out of the food court when it was discovered that she had brought a toxic blowfish.

1.5.text: Inspector Irratino used a dowsing rod and it led him directly to a saxophone at the entrance.

1.6.text: Deadly cotton candy was found in the lowest seat. And by "found," I mean Irratino saw it in a dream.

1.7.text: Inspector Irratino used his deep knowledge of cornology to derive the indisputable fact that locusts would only swarm the shortest suspect.

1.8.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a sign he had seen in the stars and then pronounced his declaration: "Leaf Collector Brown wanted to ruin the Harvest Festival."

2.1.text: Irratino reminded Logico that, when decoding the Next Letter Code, you replace every letter with the next letter in the alphabet, and you replace Z with A.

2.2.text: Irratino correctly guessed that Superfan Smoky was inside Dame Obsidian's great big house.

2.3.text: Inspector Irratino had the strongest feeling that Dame Obsidian was feeling better on the upstairs balcony.

2.4.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a dream he had dreamt and then pronounced his declaration: "The Thought of the Lily was discovered next to a translation of an Obsidian novel."

2.5.text: According to a very lengthy appendix, the Big Green Ogre was wearing the Ring of Illusion.

2.6.text: With Irratino's eyes closed, his hearing was improved, and he heard Backpacker Bisque using the rusty saw.

2.7.text: Logico could hear, as if from a great distance, Irratino telling him that a lucky slingshot was in the worst place possible.

2.8.text: Inspector Irratino was certain (with absolutely no evidence) that Crime Queen Caramel was bribing everybody to say they saw ghosts.

3.1.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a sign he had seen in the stars and then pronounced his declaration: "Admiral Navy was seen with poisoned rum."

3.2.text: Inspector Irratino examined Astrologer Azure's horoscope further and could tell that she was in one of the lifeboats.

3.3.text: Inspector Irratino examined a marot card and then declared, "Castaway Sable was in the deep blue sea." Logico was convinced he had just overheard some ship gossip.

3.4.text: Irratino's esoteric science of weatherology told him that spooky fog was rolling over the jagged rocks.

3.5.text: Inspector Irratino felt very uncomfortable being back here, so he tried to be helpful by pointing out that a fishing net was in the secluded cove.

3.6.text: Irratino saw Sailor Aero with a fish bone. So, you could say he had a vision.

3.7.text: Inspector Irratino used a dowsing rod to determine that there was seawater sludge by that big pile of metal.

3.8.text: Inspector Irratino thought that Mr. Tuxedo looked like a little cutie sitting on a chunk of ice in his formal wear.

4.1.text: Inspector Irratino picked up strong vibes that it was Major Red himself who was lying.

4.2.text: Inspector Irratino opened the Little Red Book to a random page, pointed at a word, and then used the esoteric significance of that word to conclude that the second-tallest suspect was beside a cool red banner.

4.3.text: Based on Inspector Irratino's experience with dream interpretation. it was pretty clear that a bloodstained rose was in the bedchamber.

4.4.text: Inspector Irratino could tell, from the vibes alone, that Private Perriwinkle brought a tracking device.

4.5.text: Inspector Irratino shuffled the marot and then drew two cards: Admiral Navy and a rock. Make of that what you will...

4.6.text: Inspector Irratino used the occult method of looking around to determine that Cultist Xanadu was next to some bandits.

4.7.text: Inspector Irratino shuffled his copy of the marot, threw all the cards in the air, looked at where they fell, and then declared, "Skull Collector Bleach had a copy of And Then There Was Nun."

4.8.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a map of the local ley lines and discovered—with 99.9999% certainty—that the second-tallest suspect was in a helicopter.

5.1.text: Irratino could clearly tell that this murder was motivated by selfrighteous reasons. (How he could clearly tell that, he couldn't say.)

5.2.text: Irratino ate a small leaf he found in the jungle and had a vision that a machete was in a place with dangerous vibes.

5.3.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a sign he had seen in the stars and then pronounced his declaration: "The tallest suspect was seen in yet another maze."

5.4.text: Using his deep knowledge of psychology (specifically Freudian psychology), Inspector Irratino decided that the person with a golden cup would kill if they had a claustrophobic panic attack.

5.5.text: Inspector Irratino knew—from the moment he met Archeologist Ecru—that she would absolutely, definitely, 100 percent kill someone if they murdered her wife.

5.6.text: "Logico! Keep your hand inside the mine cart. And also, High Alchemist Raven brought a big gear!"

5.7.text: Inspector Irratino knew in his heart of hearts that A-List Abalone would do anything for an audition. ANYTHING!

5.8.text: Inspector Irratino had a leaf flashback and knew immediately that, for the person in the jungle itself, if they were involved, then it was all a mirage.

6.1.text: Inspector Irratino said a quiet prayer, and immediately, the voice of the deity spoke to him and said, "An envelope of cash was in the private forest."

6.2.text: Inspector Irratino wrote a short piece of code that randomly selected items, which he felt would give the selection cosmic significance. The first result: an 80s computer was by the ominous obelisk.

6.3.text: Inspector Irratino knew just by looking at her that Agent Fuchsia had brought a pigeon.

6.4.text: Inspector Irratino drank something in the lab, passed out, and when he woke up, he knew that you needed a volumetric flask to study whatever science makes bombs.

6.5.text: Inspector Irratino drew two cards from the marot: Supreme Master Cobalt and a hypnotic pocket watch. They must go together!

6.6.text: Inspector Irratino just guessed at random that the person who doesn't have a degree was in the courtyard. And he was right!

6.7.text: Inspector Irratino could tell from the acoustics and his gut that the suspect who said, "Know it? I stole it!" was in the long hallway.

6.8.text: Inspector Irratino knew—from reading that most occult and untrustworthy of sources, the newspaper—that Technologist Turquoise was fond of his ray gun.

7.1.text: Inspector Irratino tasted a piece of the gingerbread house, and it was so delicious, he had a religious epiphany that Mrs. Ruby was an expert at making things disappear.

7.2.text: Inspector Irratino consulted a sign he had seen in the stars and then pronounced his declaration: "The person with the Skull of Golioc had a reasonable budget for crystals."

7.3.text: Inspector Irratino scryed with the pyre fire and saw, clear as day. that the person with a cauldron was handling security (and also horoscopes) for the coven.

7.4.text: Inspector Irratino drew a marot card that confirmed his preexisting opinions: The dark woods were full of hexes.

7.5.text: Irratino knew that the Skull of Golioc was in the chapel. But how he knew, he didn't know.

7.6.text: Inspector Irratino fell asleep and had a vivid dream that the person with Murdle: The Jigsaw Puzzle loved witches in the movies.

7.7.text: Inspector Irratino flipped through the magick grimoire at random, stopping on a random word, which revealed to him that Tourist Tulip's favorite magick word was "smazo." He also learned that all of these magick words were fun to say aloud.

7.8.text: Inspector Irratino drew a whole bunch of marot cards, couldn't figure out what they meant, tossed them away, and then just guessed that the tallest suspect was by the grand piano.

8.1.text: Inspector Irratino reminded Logico to look at the compass rose on the map before deciding which way was north.

8.2.text: Inspector Irratino was deeply flattered to see Dame Obsidian reading his fantasy sequel.

8.3.text: Inspector Irratino was worried the anchor would rust in that big puddle, though Logico assured him that almost all anchors were waterproof.

8.4.text: Inspector Irratino loved the spooky vibes of the Drakonian artifacts: the Skull of Dennivet went great beside Major Red's donation.

8.5.text: Inspector Irratino knew in his gut that the suspect with the Skull of Ot's favorite memory was getting paid.

8.6.text: Inspector Irratino stared into the blue screen of an old-timey computer until he saw, in its swirling CRT screen, that the person who couldn't turn a computer on or off was by a slab.

8.7.text: Inspector Irratino had a vision of Black Cat Midnight Baby in front of a huge window.

8.8.text: Inspector Irratino had read all the signs in the whole museum, and although he couldn't help with this final mystery, he had learned a lot along the way.
